chapter_theme: Deliberation ends in decision and decision must not stall; beyond that, the chapter gives a practical method of action and alliance, measured to whether one is stronger, an equal, or weaker than the other side.
structure_note: Parimelazhagar divides the chapter: general method (671-672), the three positions and the strong one's way (673-674), the equal's way (675-677), and the weak one's way (678-680).

671.reading: Deliberation ends in arriving at resolve, and it's a fault if that resolve lingers in delay.
671.nuance: The verse gives thought a limit from both sides: it must run until resolve, as Parimelazhagar notes, and it has no right to run after. Manakkudavar supplies the risk: enemies learn of the delay and take precautions.

672.reading: Sleep over what should be done slowly; do not sleep over what should be done without sleeping.
672.nuance: தூங்கு means both to sleep and to delay. The verse repeats it so that the word itself has to be sorted, and it does not tell you how to tell the two kinds of task apart; Parimelazhagar says they are known through strength and timing.

673.reading: Wherever it's possible, the deed is good; where it isn't, act by looking for a way that will go.

positions.position: வினை here means war: where stronger, fight, since force is what is feared; otherwise use one of the other three means (conciliation, division, gifts).
No reference to war: act when possible, and when not, keep it in mind and wait for an opening.
positions.quote: இயலாத காலத்து அதனை நினைந்திருந்து, இயலும் இடம் பார்த்துச் செய்க

674.reading: If you think about it, what is left over from a task or an enmity scorches like what is left over from a fire.
674.nuance: நினையுங்கால் suggests that this only becomes clear on reflection: a remainder seems small at the moment. Parimelazhagar assigns this to the stronger party, for whom leaving things unfinished seems safe.

675.reading: Act after thinking through until the darkness clears these five: resources, means, time, the deed and the place.
675.nuance: The list recalls that of 631, but both early commentators double each item: one's own and the enemy's. The verse doesn't say this, and Kalaignar's checklist has only one side. If they're right, this is a list about comparison.

676.reading: Act after looking at how it would be finished, what will hinder it, and the great yield when complete.
676.nuance: Parimelazhagar states it as a cost-benefit test: act if the yield outweighs the effort and obstacles. Manakkudavar reads முடிவு as the manner of ending, and Parimelazhagar as effort by metonymy.

677.reading: The proper way for someone doing a task is to learn the mind of the one who knows it from inside.
677.nuance: After the preceding checklists, this verse says they aren't enough, and that someone who has done it should be consulted. Parimelazhagar's உள் அறிவான் is the person who has done this before.

678.reading: Using one task to accomplish another is like binding a rutting elephant with another elephant.
678.nuance: The image takes for granted the practice of capturing elephants with an elephant, and பிணித்தல் is itself a skill of the deed. The elephants of 597 and 599 are about character; this one is about technique.

positions.position: Plan each task so that it becomes a means to finishing the next similar one.
positions.quote: தொடங்கிய வினையானே பிறிதும் ஓர் வினையை முடித்தற்கு உபாயம் ஆமாறு எண்ணிச் செய்க.

positions.position: It means setting an enemy's enemies against him, so that enmity is used against enmity.
positions.quote: தமக்கு ஒரு பகைவர் தோன்றினால் அவர்க்குப் பகையாயினாரை அவ ரோடு பகைக்குமாறு

679.reading: Bringing the unallied over to one's side is more urgent than doing good to one's friends.
679.nuance: Friends can wait because they are friends. This chilly ranking of urgency is about strategy, not love, and Parimelazhagar's reason is timing: it must be done before enemies see one's weakness.

positions.position: ஒட்டார் are those not allied with one's enemy, i.e. the enemy's enemies, to be made friends. He allows another sense: keeping one's own foes from joining others.
ஒட்டார் are simply one's enemies, to be reconciled, and this is put ahead of doing good for one's own kin.
positions.quote: தஞ் சுற்றத்திற்கு நல்லவை செய்தலினும், பகைவரைப் பொருந்தி நட்பாகக் கொள்ளுதலை

680.reading: Those whose domain is small, afraid of the trembling within, will bow to the great and accept what they can get if it is offered.
680.nuance: Parimelazhagar sees the verse's tone: since bowing isn't what the honourable would choose, கொள்வர் reports what is done, without praising it. His reason is that if one's own side panics, all is lost.

links.note: Both separate thinking from having decided. 467 condemns thinking after deciding as a disgrace, and 671 condemns delay after deciding as a fault, the one seeing it as an intellectual lapse and the other a practical one.
383 asks a ruler for தூங்காமை, sleeplessness, without condition. 672 divides this: some things should indeed be slept on. Parimelazhagar makes this connection himself.

On Parimelazhagar's reading, 673 ranks force first where one is stronger. 546 says it isn't the spear that gives victory but the king's straight sceptre. The Kural's strategy and its ethics may be speaking here to different questions. Manakkudavar's reading of 673 removes this tension.
Both warn about what enmity becomes if left to grow: 879 says fell the thorn tree young, and 674 says the left-over ember flares. 879 addresses timing, and 674 completeness.
874 says the world rests in one who can turn enmity into friendship, as a mark of character. 679 turns this into a question of scheduling: it comes before duties to friends.

969 praises those who give up life at the loss of honour, like the yak with its hair. 680 describes the weak who bow and take the terms to keep their people steady. Parimelazhagar sees this: the honourable would not choose it, so the verse only reports it.

source_issues: 672: Parimelazhagar's gloss repeats a phrase, தூங்காது செய்யும் வினை தூங்கற்க, and contains a garbled sequence. Manakkudavar's commentary is marked as not aligned.
673: The verse's first word reads ஙல்லும்வா, a typographical error for ஒல்லும்வா (as in Parimelazhagar's lemma).
680: Parimelazhagar's lemma has கொள்வார் where the verse has கொள்வர், and he later writes கொள்வர்.
